lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Owned the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards across two major releases and the on-call rotation that used them.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases, adding automated regression checks that shortened release cycles from 2 weeks to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, Kubernetes

items.says: 900 ms to 600 ms is a 33% reduction, not 50%.
items.because: Correct the 900 ms to 600 ms calculation.

items.says: 'Grouped tool-use rollouts' conflicts with 'a single rollout per prompt' and may not match GRPO's requirements.
items.because: GRPO normally requires multiple outputs in a comparison group.

items.says: 'Single-request inference' and 'dynamic batching' describe different workload conditions unless batching occurs across concurrent requests.
items.because: Resolve the inference-latency contradiction.

items.says: Reorder the experience section in reverse chronology.
items.because: The 2024–2025 internship should appear above the 2022–2024 role.

items.says: Replace or substantiate the 'AI-first engineering practices' bullet.
items.because: It is broad, promotional, and unsupported by evidence.

items.says: Reduce the density of the internship section.
items.because: Six highly technical bullets are difficult to scan; prioritize the strongest achievements.

items.says: Make the code/portfolio URL clickable and clearly identify it (e.g., as GitHub).
items.because: Ensure the link leads directly to polished, relevant work.

items.says: Add LinkedIn if it is complete and consistent with the resume.
Consider adding your current location or work authorization.
items.because: It helps employers understand your availability.

items.says: Use an en dash consistently in the date range rather than a hyphen.
Confirm that 'Expected Jun 2026' matches the university’s official expected completion date.
Consider including GPA only if it is strong and useful for the roles you are targeting.
Standardize country and location formatting across both education and experience.
Put Mobility Systems Company before Eastern Robotics Co. in experience.
items.because: Reverse chronology is standard.

items.says: Be ready to clarify whether the internship was part-time, full-time, or a co-op if the schedule could raise questions.
items.because: The internship overlaps with the master’s program.

items.says: Use US English spelling: 'Stabilised' should be 'Stabilized'.
items.because: Use consistent US English if targeting US employers.

items.says: Prevent automatic line breaks from splitting 'on-call' after 'on-'.
items.because: The current break looks like a formatting error.

items.says: Clarify what 'owned' involved and add an outcome if available.
items.because: The current wording is vague and lacks a result.

items.says: Clarify whether 'owned the on-call rotation' means operational responsibility or something else.
items.because: It is less precise than describing your actual responsibility.

items.says: Keep the two-release scope only if 'major releases' has a meaningful definition.
Clarify the test environment or production traffic profile for latency numbers.
items.because: 420 ms and 180 ms may not be production measurements.

items.says: State the traffic level or request volume if available.
items.because: Latency improvements are more credible when tied to load.

items.says: Verify that the cache did not introduce correctness or staleness tradeoffs worth mentioning.
Clarify whether the two-week and three-day figures refer to total release lead time, engineering effort, or waiting time.
State whether the regression checks covered model quality, performance, compatibility, or all three.
Clarify your individual contribution to the CI pipeline and release-cycle improvement.
items.because: Avoid over-attributing the result.

items.says: Split this bullet into at least two: technical migration and operational/people responsibilities.
items.because: It currently combines multiple accomplishments.

items.says: Explain why the event queue eliminated the backlog; clarify the causal connection.
items.because: The connection is not immediately clear.

items.says: Add scale for the queue if available, such as events per day, fleet size, or peak throughput.
Avoid implying that rewriting the logging library, onboarding hires, and taking on-call all caused the backlog result unless each actually contributed.
Clarify whether '800+ sensor signals per case' means features, measurements, channels, or time-series inputs.
Add the original backlog size or case count if available.
items.because: A 68% reduction is useful, but readers also need scale.

items.says: Clarify whether the reduction was measured against a stable baseline and whether other process changes happened during the same period.
Clarify whether you built the branch independently or as part of a team.
Define 'diagnostic accuracy' (e.g., classification accuracy, exact-match, top-k, etc.).
Clarify whether the 1,200 held-out cases were never used during model or adapter development.
'Domain adapter' is ambiguous; ensure the method is technically identifiable.
Explain the significance of 'validated tool-use trajectories.'
items.because: Clarify if validation was manual, automated, or expert-reviewed.

items.says: Keep 'assistant-only loss masking' only if it is valued by target jobs; otherwise, it may not improve recruiter comprehension.
Report uncertainty or repeated-run results for the eight-point gain if possible.
items.because: So the improvement does not appear to come from a single favorable evaluation.

items.says: Specify whether the measurement was under concurrency, sustained traffic, or a single-user benchmark.
Include the latency values, not just the percentage, if space permits.
State whether accuracy or output quality remained within an accepted tolerance after INT8 quantization.
Identify the edge hardware or hardware class if relevant.
items.because: Inference performance is hardware-dependent.

items.says: Fix the grammar: the introductory clause does not have a clear subject performing the reduction.
Clarify how GRPO training reduced end-to-end latency; make the mechanism explicit.
items.because: The connection is currently implicit.

items.says: Provide before-and-after latency values; 5% alone is modest.
Report whether accuracy, citation validity, and task completion were maintained or improved.
Consider removing this bullet if the result was not statistically or operationally meaningful.
items.because: It is one of the densest bullets and has one of the weakest outcomes.

items.says: Define the evaluation workload, because end-to-end agent latency can vary substantially by task and tool response time.
Standard GRPO relies on comparing a group of rollouts; one rollout per prompt may not provide the required signal.
items.because: Recheck the technical accuracy.

items.says: Reconcile this statement with the previous bullet’s 'grouped tool-use rollouts.'
If the comparison group was formed across prompts, trajectories, or batches, say so clearly.
Quantify 'stabilized': include a measurable reduction in divergence, variance, failed runs, reward collapse, or training restarts.
As written, this describes a method but no demonstrated benefit; add evidence or consider deletion.
Add the number or type of reviewers who adopted the runbook if that provides meaningful scale.
Add an effect if known, such as more consistent escalation, faster reviews, or fewer incorrect auto-resolutions.
Clarify whether you authored the rules or only documented rules already established by others.
Clarify whether this is an open-source, academic, personal, or internal project.
'Owner' is vague; use a role label that accurately reflects your involvement.
Link directly to the repository or deployed project if public.
'Multi-Agent Systems' is a domain; consider listing concrete frameworks, runtime, storage, or deployment tools used.
Remove or substantially change this bullet unless you can support it with specific actions and measured results.
items.because: It is broad, promotional, and unsupported by evidence.

items.says: Identify the exact practice introduced, who adopted it, and what changed.
Quantify delivery improvement or downstream impact.
Clarify what 'platform' and 'downstream teams' refer to, especially if this is a personal project.
Clarify whether result caching could return stale outputs and how cache validity was handled.
Explain the benchmark conditions, including concurrency and cache-hit rate.
Distinguish tool-result caching from reusing completed sub-agent answers if they were separate mechanisms.
Confirm that 600 ms is p95 for the same workload and hardware as the 900 ms baseline.
Change the improvement description from 12% to 12 percentage points; the relative improvement is about 16.9%.
Define the benchmark suite: number of tasks, task types, and whether it is public or custom.
Clarify how task completion was scored and whether the improvement held across multiple runs.
Mention any latency or cost tradeoff from retries.
items.because: Retries often improve success at the expense of both.

items.says: Explain safeguards against repeatedly retrying invalid or unrecoverable sub-agent calls.
Clarify the project’s affiliation and provide a repository or contribution link if public.
Verify that all eight metrics were accepted upstream and currently run by default.
Name the metric categories or evaluation dimensions if not obvious from 'citation and faithfulness.'
If the project is recognizable, include its name or repository rather than describing it generically.
Be prepared to distinguish metrics you designed from metrics you implemented.
Specify which Kendall statistic was used (e.g., tau or tau-b).
Explain what was ranked and what the evaluator’s scores were compared against.
Clarify whether the 400+ trials were independent and how many original reports were used.
Describe the degradation levels or severity ordering enough to establish that 0.89 is meaningful.
Include statistical uncertainty or significance if available.
Clarify what 'defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling' means operationally.
Explain the impact of each defect or the most important defect.
'To their modules' is difficult to parse; make the debugging scope and root-cause identification clearer.
If each fix was accepted upstream, link the relevant issues or pull requests in the project materials.
Quantify the improvement after the fixes if it was measured.
Move Git out of 'Programming'; it is a development tool, not a programming language.
Add other languages only if you can use them in an interview.
Move Kubernetes to a tools, infrastructure, cloud, or deployment category.
Separate training techniques from libraries and domains; PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation, and Kubernetes are not the same type of skill.
Consider whether 'agent evaluation' is specific enough.
items.because: Your project bullets demonstrate more precise evaluation capabilities.

items.says: Add technologies already evidenced by the resume—CI/CD, event queues, caching, model serving, quantization, or observability—only where you can name the actual tools and discuss them confidently.
Include databases, cloud platforms, containers, Linux, and testing frameworks only if you have genuine experience with them.
Avoid listing highly specialized terms such as GRPO if the corresponding bullets remain technically ambiguous.
Use en dashes consistently for all date ranges.
Keep spelling consistently American or British; US-targeted applications should use American spelling.
Ensure no hyphenated term breaks awkwardly across lines.
Keep bullet lengths more uniform; several bullets currently span four or more lines and contain multiple accomplishments.
Consider limiting each position to roughly four or five high-value bullets.
Verify every percentage, denominator, and causal claim.
items.because: Preserve the quantitative style, but ensure accuracy.

items.says: Make project and open-source links visible and clickable without relying on generic URL text.
